caption: The drawing consists of three views of a single three-legged object, depicted in grayscale pencil shading on an off-white background. At the top of the drawing is a plan (top-down) view, showing the object as a roughly triangular shape composed of three wide, slightly curved arms joined at the corners and converging at one point. Directly beneath this view is a scale bar with labeled increments marked “0 1 2,” representing units of measurement. Below the scale bar is a side (profile) view, illustrating the object’s structure as it stands on three legs, each leg sweeping downward at the ends with a rounded profile. At the bottom of the page is a perspective view, showing the object as a three-legged frame with thick, tubular arms that converge at an elevated central point and descend to form the three legs. The shading in all three views gives the object a sense of volume and solidity, with darker tones used to emphasize curves and thickness. The background is otherwise blank, focusing all attention on the depicted object and its three-dimensional form.
title: Trivet
